original_card.question: Can a specified pair of consecutive calls eliminate a restoration that the next call reconstructs?
methods: Write typed entry/exit contracts and a contracting multitype recurrence.
Derive a lower bound for the compulsory transitions of one proposed typed interface.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Show actual eliminated work and legal composition; changing a scalar recurrence into a matrix is insufficient.

first_step.inspect: Find a concrete consecutive-call boundary in the selected review and list its entry/exit obligations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Specify two call types and one operation actually removed by composition; derive the normalized recurrence.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Eliminating compulsory boundary work can lower recursive cost beyond packing gains.
allowed_variations: A two-type pilot or one explicit deferred restoration.
scope_change_triggers: Rewriting the old scalar recurrence as a matrix without eliminating work.

actual_scope: For every n>=2 over F2, share the dirty connector across x'=x+Cu when B1=J_n, B1C=0, and B2=B1+R is rank one; canonical finite instance C=e0+e1,R=E00, with a proof extension to every nonzero even-weight C and unit R=E_(i,j) where C_j=1.
scope_change_reason: The catalogue asks whether a pair can remove repeated restoration. This refinement changes both the source and the connector map: after x becomes x+Cu, a rank-one delta R changes B to B+R. The earlier same-map BC adapter does not cover this source-dependent correction.
bottleneck_link: The paired schedule removes one complete B update and one complete B' update, paying the explicit rank-one R update instead. It can reduce the relevant paid interface cost exactly when c_B+c_B' exceeds c_R plus any additional setup/admission cost; no selected recursive tariff is instantiated.
stop_rule: Complete the general dirty-state identity, exact direct-row invoice, exhaustive state checks for n=2..5 and three negative controls. Stop before searching for a selected-supplier caller; carry that as the next bounded question and make no kappa claim.
evidence: PROOF.md gives the general dirty-connector correction (B1+B2)x' + B1Cu and the all-n J_n family. verify.py checks the general identity on all 32,768 2x2 map/source/dirty-input cases and the even-C/unit-R family on 444,800 transition states; checks literal factored gate lists and reversed inverses on 180 basis columns across n=2..5; and checks direct, paired, connector-restored and strict schedules on all 2,236,928 arbitrary dirty x,u,z,y1,y2 inputs for n=2..5. It rejects four negative controls, including omission of the general B1 C u correction when B1 C is nonzero. At n=4 the strongest connector-restored baseline is 44+p_t versus 36+p_t for the paired schedule; strict independent calls cost 52+p_t. The direct row-add bill is 80->50. These are local XOR-model results only; selected supplier integration is absent.
author: Cinna Davis, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance
ai_assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted with overlap research, construction derivation, verifier implementation, exact cost accounting, package text and validation. No external code or unverified prior implementation was imported.

open_questions.why_it_matters: Only a concrete caller with complete typed prices can show whether this local interface mechanism lowers a selected paid recursive moment.
open_questions.first_step: Extract one pair of complete call contracts from the current selected source and solve the exact equations B_old C=0 and rank(B_new-B_old)=1 before building a schedule.
open_questions.blocked_by: No selected owner/call pair has been identified; any candidate must still pay source access, matrix updates, scratch, frames, dispatch, routing, restoration, hosting and precision.

bounded_experiment.object: Two sequential dirty-connector readouts with scalar source update x'=x+Cu and map change R=B1+B2 over F2.
bounded_experiment.hypothesis: If B1 C=0 and rank(R)=1, applying the exact correction R x' can replace closing B1 and reopening B2; the proof identifies the general unique correction R x'+B1 C u.
bounded_experiment.domain: Uniform proof for n>=2, including the even-weight C / unit-map-delta extension; complete 2x2 general correction identity; 444,800 small even-C/unit-R transition states; exhaustive dirty states for the canonical J_n,C=e0+e1,R=E00 family at n=2..5.
bounded_experiment.optimistic_fully_charged_local_bill: At n=4, after granting both schedules one shared clean parity bit at the same full cost p_t, the baseline that restores the connector between outputs costs 44+p_t ADDs and the paired schedule 36+p_t; net save 8. Strict independent calls cost 52+p_t. Every parity, map-delta, source, readout, restoration and scratch-uncompute gate is counted; supplier/host costs are excluded from this local model and must enter c_patch or Delta_I.
bounded_experiment.stop_condition: Stop after the general identity, the fixed family, exact gate schedules, exhaustive checks and negative controls; do not search selected supplier integration in this cycle.

cost_model_pivot: The first concrete bill used direct matrix-entry ADDs. Since J_n is rank one, replace it as the headline comparison with an explicit parity-factor circuit; strengthen the baseline by allowing the same parity bit to persist across the pair while requiring the connector to close after each output. The net saving is then 2n, with p_t charged equally.
